items.title: A common local basin
items.note: For F : Vec n → ℝ convex with unique minimizer x* (hmin, huniq): every sublevel {F ≤ c} is compact; for every U ∈ 𝓝 x* there is ε > 0 with {F ≤ F(x*)+ε} ⊆ U and every admissible run with F(x_0) ≤ F(x*)+ε stays in U (ε is chosen before the run R, hence independently of H_0). No n ≥ 1 is needed for the lemma itself.

The library proof follows the paper (positive gap on a sphere, radial lower bound by convexity, ε = gap/2); it works in any finite-dimensional normed space, so with the sup norm of Vec n; the displays are stated with the Euclidean norm of the paper.

δ is a variable with defining equation δ = sInf {F(x*+u) − F(x*) : ‖u‖ = r} (Euclidean norm ‖euclideanVector u‖); the theorem proves that this infimum is a minimum (IsLeast) and is positive. Standing assumptions: the lemma's, U ∈ 𝓝 x*, r > 0 with the closed Euclidean ball B̄_r(x*) ⊆ U. The sphere is nonempty only for n ≥ 1: hn : 1 ≤ n is the article's convention (Definition art:admissible, n ≥ 1); the lemma's statement does not repeat it.
Under the assumptions of disp/001 (δ as defined there), for every x with ‖x − x*‖ ≥ r (Euclidean).

PositivePartition.polyhedral is proved by the library's finite_polyhedral_basin → local_cells_basin, which follows this proof: discard the cells not containing x* and shrink (incident_neighborhood), radial derivative equality and local Taylor bounds give the inward condition on compact sets in the ball (local_cells_inward), then Lemma art:localization and the radial convergence corollary. Notation: r is both the radius of B_r(x*) and, in r_x, the global.tex vector r_x = x − x*; the Lean statements write r for the radius and x − xstar for r_x.

Stated under the theorem's hypotheses plus the objects of local.tex:49-57: the Euclidean ball B = B_r(x*) (hB) with B ⊆ U and B ⊆ V_i for every cell containing x* (hBU, hBV), the discarded cells (hdisc: every cell meeting B contains x*), a common Lipschitz bound L ≥ 0 of the remaining extension gradients on B (hLip, Euclidean norms), a differentiability point x ∈ B with gradient g, and a cell P_i ∋ x. ∇f_i(x) is coordinateGradient (f i) x.

Same standing assumptions as disp/003, for 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1 (the inward segment of local.tex:59); ‖r_x‖² is sqNorm (x − xstar). The middle inequality is the sharp Taylor bound f(y) − f(x) − ∇f(x)^T(y−x) ≤ (L/2)‖y−x‖² for an L-Lipschitz gradient (taylor_upper_of_lipschitz, proved here; the library's taylor_remainder_le has the constant L instead of L/2).

items.title: Smooth losses with polyhedral or quadratic pieces
items.note: Piecewise linear-quadratic is the meaning fixed in the proof (local.tex:85-86): F(x) = x^T Q_i x + c_i^T x + d_i on each cell of a finite cover of ℝⁿ by closed full-dimensional polyhedra P_i = {x | a_ij^T x ≤ b_ij}. 'Has the local convergence property of Theorem art:polyhedral' is stated for every open neighborhood U of x* (the representation is global, so the theorem applies with any U): ∃ ε > 0, chosen before the run, with x_k ∈ U, F(x_k) → F(x*), x_k → x* for every admissible run with F(x_0) ≤ F(x*)+ε. plq is the first sentence; plq_loss_regularizer the second (loss convex and locally C^{1,1} on ℝⁿ, regularizer convex and PLQ, F = loss + reg with a unique minimizer). Full-dimensionality (_hfull) is not used.

The proof's sentence 'By piecewise linear-quadratic we mean ...' is a definition used in the statement of plq (see the corollary's note); quadratic_eq identifies the library's quadratic Q c d with x^TQx + c^Tx + d.

items.title: A local centered-composite basin
items.note: 'The representation and smoothness assumptions of Theorem art:centered hold on a neighborhood of x*' is read with the set U of Theorem art:centered taken as a neighborhood of x*: U open and convex, x* ∈ U, ψ convex and locally C^{1,1} on U, γ finite, convex and positively homogeneous of degree one (Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne γ: γ(t•x) = t γ(x) for t ≥ 0), F = ψ + γ(· − x*) on U, x* the unique minimizer. Convexity of U (_hUc) is not used beyond ConvexOn ℝ U ψ.
The library proof follows the paper: localization, compact initial sublevel in U, Theorem art:centered (centered_values).

The display defines ψ and γ (variables with these defining equations; Σ_{i∉I_0} is the sum over the complement I0ᶜ) and asserts F(x) = ψ(x) + γ(x − x*) on the open convex neighborhood N = {σ_i x_i > 0, i ∉ I_0} of local.tex:120 (see prose/012). Standing assumptions of local.tex:115-121: A ∈ ℝ^{m×n}, b ∈ ℝ^m, λ > 0, x* the unique minimizer, I_0 = {i : x*_i = 0}, σ_i = sign(x*_i) (Real.sign) for i ∉ I_0.

C_aff is {p | IsAffineCritical F p}. The library predicate is stated with the Euclidean copy euclideanVector '' ∂F(p); affineCritical_set_eq unfolds C_aff to {p | 0 ∈ affineSpan ℝ (subdifferential F p)}, i.e. 0 ∈ aff ∂F(p), where subdifferential F p = {g | ∀ z, g^T(z − p) ≤ F z − F p} (mem_subdifferential).

items.title: An affine-critical cluster point in the plane
items.note: F_* is Fstar with IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar (attained minimum). Hypothesis 1 is stated literally with frontier. Hypothesis 2 is stated literally (F is C² on an open neighborhood of p, or F = max{f₁,f₂} on an open neighborhood V of p where f₁, f₂ are convex and C² on V, both active at p, with linearly independent gradients); regular_of_paper converts it to the library's ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p ∨ PlanarCornerCharts.ConvexTwoBranchRegularAt F p (paper_of_regular is the converse). 'Starting in K' is R.x 0 ∈ {F ≤ b}; a cluster point is MapClusterPt p atTop R.x. The hypotheses _hF (convexity is also part of AdmissibleBFGSRun) and _hb (b > F_*) are not needed by the Lean proof. The library proof differs from the paper's in the transport bookkeeping (|log λ_k| ≤ C d_k and a scalar energy instead of λ_k² ≤ 1 + L d_k); the paper's steps are covered by disp/007-009. Non-vacuity, with an actual admissible run starting in K: the Local module's example for F(u,v) = u² + |v| (b = 1, the library's UnexcitedMetric.run), which also covers planar_convergence, disp/007 and disp/009.

The library theorems listed state the undisplayed steps: ℓ > F_* when no cluster point is affine critical, steps tending to zero under strict contours, constancy of F on the limit segment and its position in the boundary, and the final energy contradiction (the O(N) reciprocal bound against Theorem art:reciprocal-growth). Notation: in display 008 the letter t is the curvature y^T s while in hypothesis 1 of the theorem t is a level; β and C are reused from other sections. Attribution 'exactly as in the proof of Theorem art:certificate' (local.tex:270) is correct (energy.tex:302-308).

Stated under the theorem's hypotheses for the run R starting in K, for every k and 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1; the proof uses it along a subsequence x_k → x, x_{k+1} → z ≠ x (the subsequence and the contradiction hypothesis are not needed). d_k = α_k q_k = R.d k.

Standing assumptions at this point: the theorem's hypotheses, the run R starting in K, its value limit ℓ, the contradiction hypothesis (no cluster point is affine critical) and ℓ > F_*; they cannot all hold (that is the theorem). The Lean proof applies the library's all-pair form of Lemma art:planar-field (item A/planar_geometry/lemma/art:planar-field) to the compact cluster set Γ at level ℓ and shrinks δ so that d ≤ 1 (the lemma gives λ² ≤ 1 + Ld for d ≤ 1, and sufficiently close pairs have d ≤ ‖g‖‖s‖ ≤ 1 by the subgradient bound on the compact buffer); m = η², C = C₀, L = C'. 'Sufficiently close' is ‖s‖ < δ (Euclidean); eligibility is for the run's constants c1, c2; g = ∇F(x), h = ∇F(z), s = z − x, y = h − g, t = y^Ts, d = −g^Ts.

E_k = w(x_k)^T H_k^{-1} w(x_k) is a variable with its defining equation; λ_k, β_k, m, C, L are variables with the four properties that disp/008 gives for the accepted pair (x_k, x_{k+1}) of the tail. 'The parenthesized quadratic form is nonnegative' (local.tex:268) is scalar_frame_residual_nonneg.

items.title: When affine criticality is correct
items.note: Under the hypotheses of planar_cluster plus C_aff ∩ K ⊆ argmin F: for every admissible run starting in K, F(x_k) → F_*, the Euclidean distance to argmin F tends to 0 (euclideanSolutionDistance), and if argmin F = {x*} then x_k → x*. Its hypotheses, including C_aff ∩ K ⊆ argmin F, hold with an actual admissible run starting in K (the Local module's example for F(u,v) = u² + |v|, b = 1, UnexcitedMetric.run).
The library proof follows the paper (an affine-critical cluster point is optimal; compactness gives distance and uniqueness conclusions).

items.title: Nondegenerate planar smooth maxima
items.note: 'Near x*, F = max_i f_i with convex C² branches' is an open U ∋ x* on which the f_i are convex and C² and F(x) is the largest f_i(x) (IsGreatest). The contour hypothesis is ∃ b > F_* with no boundary segments for F_* < t ≤ b. I_* = {i : f_i(x*) = F(x*)} with the gradient family and the weights indexed by I_* itself; F_* = F(x*). The last sentence is planar_max_hessian_contours: a common bound ∇²f_i − μI ⪰ 0 (μ > 0) on U for the active branches i ∈ I_* (the 'locally relevant branches'; RadialHessian.matrix is the matrix of the second Fréchet derivative) implies the contour hypothesis. active_family_conversion translates to the library's Fin-enumeration of I_*.
Hypotheses hpos, hsum, hzero of planar_max (weights indexed by I_*).
The conclusion of planar_max (∃ ε > 0 before ∀ R).

Undisplayed steps: discarding inactive branches (localFiniteMax_restrict_active), 'this expression is continuous and equals λ* at x*' (local.tex:329, planar_max_balance_continuous), nearby affine-critical points are minimizers and keep all of I_* active (planar_max_affine_correct_near), at most two active branches and the regular two-branch chart away from affine criticality (planar_max_regular_near), strict convexity of the maximum under the Hessian bound (strictConvexOn_finite_max). The proof's description of ∂F(p) of a finite smooth maximum (local.tex:330-338) is the library's local_affine_critical_correctness.

A(x) is a variable with its defining equation (the 3 × |I_*| matrix with columns (∇f_i(x), 1), i ∈ I_*). The theorem also states the preceding sentence: A(x*) has full column rank by affine independence and this persists near x*; there every solution of A(p)λ = (0,0,1)^T equals (A(p)^TA(p))^{-1}A(p)^T(0,0,1)^T.

items.title: Convergence with curved, nonradial switching
items.note: f_i and F are variables with the defining equations of disp/013 (u = x 0, v = x 1); example_eq identifies them with PlanarQuadraticExample.branch/objective. The convergence part is the library's fullBFGS_explicit_basin, which applies the general planar theorem (planar_convergence_on_sublevel; its hypotheses hold for this F, see the non-vacuity example of the Local module). The failure part is stated explicitly: for every neighborhood N₀ of 0 there is η > 0 such that for every C some differentiable pair x, z ∈ N₀ with F(0)+η ≤ F(z) ≤ F(x), T = (h−g)^T(z−x) > 0 violates N² ≤ CT, N = (h−g)^T z (r_z = z, x* = 0); this negates (art:radial-condition) (A/global/disp/002) on N₀, for every C (not only C ≥ 0); the same pairs are eligible for c1 = 1/4, c2 = 1/2 (EligiblePair). The library's PlanarQuadraticSeparationTarget (planarQuadraticSeparation) also gives a realizing SPD H with bfgsStep H g 1 = z − x. Non-vacuity of the run part: PlanarQuadraticExample.nonradial_example_nonvacuous (bfgs_lean_article/BfgsArticle/AdmissibleRunExistence.lean, same hypotheses hf, hF) gives, for every H₀ ≻ 0 and all 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1, an infinite admissible run with F(x₀) < 1/100 (x₀ = (1/1000, 0)) whose values and iterates converge to 0. It applies the general AdmissibleRunExistence.exists_admissible_run (convex, bounded below, differentiable at all but countably many points of every line through a point of differentiability, no point of differentiability with gradient zero).
The defining equations hf (f_0, f_1, f_2 in u = x 0, v = x 1) and hF (F = max_i f_i) of nonradial_example and of the display theorems of its proof.

Every quantitative claim of the proof was checked in Lean: Hessians between I and 3I, (f_0+f_1+f_2)/3 = u²+v², F ≥ u²+v², unique minimizer 0, strict positive contours, active gradients (1,0),(0,1),(−1,−1) with weights 1/3 (example_model_facts); D = 3(1+v−uv) is the determinant of the augmented gradient matrix (rows ∂_u, ∂_v, 1), D ≥ 267/100 and the numerators ≥ 23/100, 49/100, 45/100 on |u|,|v| ≤ 1/10, coefficients sum to one with zero weighted gradient, affine independence, affine correctness and regularity on the box, {F ≤ 1/100} in the box (example_box_facts); the positive tie with f_2 inactive (example_tie); Δ/d → 1/2 and t/d → 1 as u, e → 0⁺ (example_ratio_limits); eventual eligibility, y^Tz → u²/2 − v² ≠ 0, t → 0⁺, unbounded quotient and the fixed band (library, used in eligible_radial_unbounded_on_neighborhood). All hold.
For every solution λ of Σλ_i = 1, Σλ_i∇f_i(x) = 0 (Cramer's rule; D need not be nonzero), with D = 3(1+v−uv) a variable with its defining equation.
v is a variable with the displayed defining equation; the expansion is as u → 0⁺ (the proof fixes u > 0). The library also proves |v(u) − u + u²/2| ≤ u³ for 0 < u < 1/10.
At (u, v(u)); 'for small u' is 0 < u < 1/10 (where u²/2 − v² < 0).

For fixed 0 < u < 1/10 and all sufficiently small e > 0 (∀ᶠ e in 𝓝[>] 0): unique activity of branches 1 and 0 at x and z (the sentence before the display), g = ∇F(x) = ∇f_1(x), h = ∇F(z) = ∇f_0(z), and the three identities.
